Subject: VPC pricing and support tiers — follow up

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the demo last week — PulseHealth is very interested in a VPC/on‑prem option for our inference workloads. Before we loop procurement formally, can you confirm a few commercial points so we can include them in the RFP?

1) Platform fee: is this a one‑time license or an annual/platform subscription? How is it amortized for multi‑year deals?
2) On‑prem vs VPC licensing: are there different SKUs or is it the same license with different deployment entitlements? Any caps on cores/GPU counts?
3) Support tiers: what is included in Standard vs Enterprise (SLA, on‑call, response times)? Are 24x7 P1 escalation and on‑site assistance available as add‑ons?
4) Discounts / migration credits: we have a competitive procurement process. What level of concession can you offer for a 12‑24 month committed GPU month contract?

Attaching a short RFP summary we circulated internally. We need a tidy one‑page commercial summary to include in the procurement packet by Friday.

Pulse_RFP_summary.pdf (attachment stub)

Hi Alice — great to hear; appreciate the RFP summary. Quick answers below and a high‑level commercial snapshot attached. Happy to refine after a short call.

Summary (high level) — commercial options:
• Platform fee: typically an annual platform subscription when deployed as VPC (recurring), or a multi‑year amortized license for on‑prem (we can amortize as CAPEX-friendly schedule). Standard annual: $75,000/year listed; 24‑month pricing can be amortized to reduce per‑year impact.
• Licensing model: same core license across VPC and on‑prem. Differences are in deployment entitlements and managed control plane options — e.g., private control plane vs fully managed hosted control plane. We cap at agreed GPU pools per contract (we'll define a committed GPU‑month SKU).
• Support tiers: Standard = business hours, 4‑hour P1 response SLAs; Enterprise = 24x7 with 1‑hour P1 response, named technical lead, quarterly architecture reviews. On‑site assistance is available as a billable add‑on or included for certain enterprise packages.
• Discounts / credits: baseline commercial guidance — 12‑month committed GPU usage: up to 15% discount on unit rates + 1 month migration credit (one‑time). 24‑month commit: up to 25% discount + 1.5 months migration credit. We can substitute migration credit for an equivalent one‑time invoice credit.

I've attached a short CommercialSummary_v1.xlsx that maps platform fee, support tier pricing, and an example line for a 50 GPU‑month commitment. Two optional concessions we can consider: a front‑loaded migration credit (one‑time) or an increased discount in exchange for a longer invoice commitment.

If you want to push for a lower platform fee, we usually trade that for a longer commitment length or a higher support revenue commitment.

Propose 30m tomorrow to lock down the numbers for procurement — what times work?

Attachments: CommercialSummary_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Customer Success – Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
